Plus that adds the excitement of discovering things together, since you'll all be new to it.

I've almost certainly clocked more than 300 games in the 13 months I've had Sentinels (playing online means I get in more games than the "average" player), and like Ronway I'm nowhere near burnout. There has to be literally billions of different hero/villain/environment combinations, and even with the exact same setup you'll see different cards and a different game. Not to mention promos...

I believe randomising everything helps a lot. If you always play Haka or prefer to take Tempest every time you face Voss, you're more likely to get bored.

posts.name: Isotope-X
posts.cooked:
You can certainly try to pick a different way to set up the game--if you typically choose characters, go random.  If you typically pick randomly, instead try to select thematic set-ups.

 

You can also try the campaign variants that people have created (boardgamegeek.com has some in their forums) where you play a linked series of games and success or failure affect future games.  There are also variant heroes and villains to try (with some variation in quality).

 

Of course, you may have already done these things, in which case try another game for a while.  Legendary is probably the best super-hero themed game (other than SOTM of course) right now.  I recently picked up the Mage Knight board game and it's spectacular, but be ready for long games.  Or check out some of the "modern classics" like Carcasonne, Settlers of Catan, Puerto Rico, or Agricola.

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
Now I know everyone loves Settlers, but I want to say right now that I hate that game.

My recommendation for a non-Sentinels game for people who like Sentinels would probably be Flash Point: Fire Rescue. It's a co-op where you really have to work together to win, and it isn't as prone to alpha player syndrome (i.e. one experienced player controlling everyone) as say, Pandemic. Plus it has genuine tension and moments of both panic and relief.

posts.name: Matchstickman
posts.cooked:
Ronway:

I'm fairly certain I have played well over a thousand games within my 2 and half years of playing, and I have yet encountered a time where I am tired of playing Sentinels of the Multiverse. The complete opposite is actually true, I wish I had more time to play more.

Today was a monthly gaming thing that pwaston, Ameena and I meet at, we spent 6 hours playing SotM and I played the same character all day*. I am not burnt out.

 

 

  • I wanted to try and play the same character all day to see if it felt different each time I played, I picked a complexity 1 character for this experiment. I felt the first 2 games went the same way, I was looking for the same combination both times. While in later games I did get the same cards it was not always the best play to try and get 'teh uber combo' to go off and I played other cards. Despite playing a single hero all day I never felt underwhelmed by my choices and think I played every card in the deck at least once  (by choice)  during the course of the games. It was an interesting experiment but not one I feel I shall be repeating.
